hook.title: React ships 4× more JavaScript for the same app.
hook.lede: Keep JSX, function components and TypeScript. Lose the re-render: a Pyreon component runs once, and a signal updates only the DOM node that reads it, so there is nothing to memoise and no dependency array to get wrong.

rows.pyreon: The component body runs once; a signal change re-runs only the bindings that read it.
rows.rival: The component function re-runs on every state change; `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `memo` limit the cost.

rows.pyreon: No concurrent scheduler: updates are synchronous and touch only the changed nodes.
rows.rival: Transitions and deferred values let React interrupt and prioritise rendering.

rows.pyreon: 77 first-party packages (router, forms, query, charts, flow, table, i18n…); React libraries that use only public hooks can run through `@pyreon/react-compat`.
rows.rival: A far larger third-party catalog: component kits, React Flow, react-aria and thousands more, all running as-is.
Over a decade in production and the largest hiring pool in front-end.

rows.pyreon: The same `.tsx` compiles to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose with PMTC (experimental).
rows.rival: React Native shares the language and the model; it is production-grade.

code.title: The same search box, twice.
code.caption: Both filter a list as you type. The React version re-runs the whole function on every keystroke and memoises to stay fast. The Pyreon version runs once; the input, the count and the list each update on their own.

rival.label: React 19

pyreon.label: Pyreon

code.checked: React side: typechecked with `@types/react` 19.3 under `tsc --strict`. Pyreon side: typechecked against the repo's `tsconfig` (0 errors), compiled with the real JSX compiler (`transformJSX`) and mounted in happy-dom; typing into the input filters the list.

items.instead: `computed(fn)`: it tracks what it reads, so there is no dependency list.
A plain function. The component runs once, so the closure is created once.
Nothing. A parent update never re-runs a child component.
None, anywhere. `effect` and `computed` subscribe to the signals they read.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick React
items: Your app leans on React-only libraries (a component kit, React Flow, react-aria) and swapping them is not on the plan.
You need concurrent rendering: transitions that interrupt work, deferred values.
Hiring and a long production record weigh more for you than bundle size or update cost.
You share code with a React Native app that ships today.

migrate.title: Bring your React app with you.
migrate.text: Point `react` at `@pyreon/react-compat`, keep shipping, and convert one component at a time.
